title: Stooking the Sheaves

readiness.math: equal groups: so many groups of so many (early multiplication)
readiness.reading: pre-reader friendly; all text can be read aloud

intro.speaker: hannah
intro.text: Welcome to the farm! The wheat is cut, and tied in bundles called sheaves.

intro.speaker: hannah
intro.text: We stand them up in little groups, called stooks, so they can dry in the sun. Three sheaves to a stook!

steps.speaker: hannah
steps.prompt: Put three sheaves in each stook. Count: one, two, three.
steps.hint: Find a stook with an empty dip, and stand a sheaf there.

older.prompt: Four sheaves in each stook this time, and five stooks. No dips: count them yourself.

feedback.full: That stook has its sheaves. Try the next one.
feedback.all_good: Four stooks of three: twelve sheaves, drying in the sun!

outro.speaker: hannah
outro.text: Twelve sheaves, in four groups of three. Bread for many families, from one field!

journal_line: I stood the wheat sheaves in stooks with Mrs. Hannah.
unavailable_text: The sheaves are standing for today.
